h1: The 7 Best Small Printers for Home Offices of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Small Home Office Printers: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: seven compact printers for home offices, from slim inkjets to mono lasers, compared on footprint, duplex, feeder and ink costs.
summary: The Canon PIXMA TS6520 is our top pick for a one-person desk because it packs print, scan and copy with auto duplex into a compact body. The Brother DCP-L2640DW is the pick if you print mostly text and want a laser. The Canon PIXMA TR4720 adds a feeder and fax for paper-heavy work, and the Epson WF-2930 is a feature-rich budget buy.
intro: Small printers hide a trap: the smaller the body, the more the maker leans on ink or toner for profit. A tiny printer that dries out between uses or locks you into a subscription is a bigger problem on a quiet home desk than a few extra inches of width.

We reviewed seven compact machines suited to a spare room, a shelf or a corner of a desk, and ranked them on size, features that matter for a single worker, and what they ask of you in ink, toner or plans. Findings come from listing specs and product claims, with no suggestion of lab or room trials.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TS6520 Wireless Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: A compact all-in-one with a small OLED screen and automatic two-sided printing.
products.description:
The TS6520 is a compact color inkjet that prints, scans and copies, with a 1.42 inch OLED display and automatic duplex. Its speed and queue handling are tuned for one user.

It ranks first because the screen makes everyday tasks easier than on screenless rivals, and it is cheaper than a laser. The TS4320 style models drop the display, which is the main difference.

Buy it for a single person working from home who wants a full set of office functions in a small body. The caveat is that it has no document feeder.
products.idealFor: A solo worker wanting full functions in a small body.

products.name: Brother DCP-L2640DW Wireless Compact Monochrome Laser Multi-Function
products.verdict: A fast mono laser that handles duplex, copy and scan for shared offices.
products.description:
The DCP-L2640DW is a compact black-and-white laser that does duplex printing, copying and scanning, and its page output is faster than an inkjet all-in-one. Toner does not dry out between uses.

It ranks second because that no-dry-out trait suits a home office that prints in bursts. It draws more standby power than an inkjet and costs more upfront, in the $200-500 bucket.

Choose it for a home office shared by two or three people. The caveat is the lack of color.
products.idealFor: Shared home offices printing reliable text.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TR4720 All-in-One Wireless Printer
products.verdict: A compact color inkjet that adds an automatic feeder and fax.
products.description:
The TR4720 is a compact all-in-one with an automatic document feeder and built-in fax, set up through the Canon PRINT app. It is designed around a single user.

It ranks third because the feeder is a rare find at this size and price, while the TS6520 has the nicer display. For paperwork, the feeder matters more.

Get it if you occasionally scan or fax multi-page documents. The caveat is that cartridge costs add up if you print a lot.
products.idealFor: Home offices that scan or fax stacks of pages.
products.skipIf: You want a display or color-heavy printing.

products.name: Epson Workforce WF-2930 Wireless All-in-One Printer
products.verdict: Feeder, duplex, fax and a color screen without laser pricing.
products.description:
The WF-2930 offers an automatic document feeder, duplex printing, fax, scan and copy, with a 1.4 inch color screen. It is a cartridge-based inkjet.

It ranks fourth because it is the most feature-rich inkjet at its price, but cartridge refills are costlier over time than a laser or tank. The TR4720 has a similar feeder and fax set for the same bucket.

Buy it for a single-user home office that wants every feature without paying laser prices. The caveat is running costs.
products.idealFor: One-person offices wanting every feature cheaply.
products.skipIf: You print a lot and want low running costs.

products.name: Brother HL-L2405W Wireless Compact Monochrome Laser Printer
products.verdict: A tiny laser that only prints, works with Alexa, and uses retail toner.
products.description:
The HL-L2405W is a compact black-and-white laser that prints only, supports Alexa, and takes toner cartridges that are sold at retail. There is no scan or copy function.

It ranks fifth because the missing scanner limits it to one job. For the $100-200 bucket, it is the neatest way to get crisp text out of a very small body.

Choose it if all you need is documents on paper. The caveat is that you will need another device for scanning.
products.idealFor: Writers and remote workers printing text only.
products.skipIf: You need to scan or copy.

products.name: HP DeskJet 4355 Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: A compact color all-in-one with a three-month ink plan trial.
products.description:
The DeskJet 4355 is a compact color inkjet all-in-one that includes a three-month trial of HP's Instant Ink plan and is set up through the HP Smart app.

It ranks sixth because the ink arrives on a subscription after the trial, which some people dislike. The upside is a low-cost way to test whether the plan suits you.

Pick it if you want to try subscription ink. The caveat is that ongoing ink depends on that plan.
products.idealFor: People curious about an ink subscription.

products.name: Epson EcoTank ET-2400 Wireless Color All-in-One Printer
products.verdict: Cartridge-free tanks last months, though the body is bigger.
products.description:
The ET-2400 uses a cartridge-free supertank system and prints, scans and copies in color. Its tanks last months without a refill, and cost per page is low.

It ranks last in this small-printer list only because the body is larger than the cartridge machines. For a home office that prints regularly, it is the cheapest to run.

Choose it when you print color often and have a shelf big enough. The caveat is the footprint.
products.idealFor: Regular printers who have a bit of space.

whatMatters.detail: A small printer must fit your desk or shelf. Ink tank models like the Epson ET-2400 are larger than cartridge inkjets. Check the dimensions in the specs and measure your space.
Lasers print text fast and toner does not dry out, while inkjets handle color but can clog if idle. Look at the printer type in the title and consider how often you print.
An automatic feeder scans multi-page originals unattended. It matters if you handle contracts or forms. Look for 'ADF' or 'automatic document feeder' in the bullets.
Subscription ink can lower cost for some and frustrate others. The HP DeskJet 4355 includes a three-month trial. Read the listing for the plan terms before buying.
A small screen simplifies tasks, while app setup eases installation. The TS6520 has a 1.42 inch OLED. Check for a display in the specs.

cards.label: Inkjet
cards.text: The Canon TS6520 and TR4720, Epson WF-2930 and HP DeskJet 4355 print color, though ink can dry out when idle.

cards.label: Laser
cards.text: The Brother DCP-L2640DW and HL-L2405W print mono text quickly and the toner does not dry out between uses.

howToChoose.note: Most home offices should default to an inkjet, the Canon TS6520, unless they print mainly black text.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A compact chassis that fits a shelf or desk corner and does not need much clearance.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The Brother HL-L2405W and Canon TS6520 are the compact choices, while the Epson ET-2400 has the bigger body.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You print often and reliability matters, so the Brother DCP-L2640DW or Epson ET-2400 pay back in upkeep.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You print occasionally. The Canon TS6520 or TR4720 covers it for less.

faq.q: Will a small printer fit on a desk?
faq.a: Most compact inkjets do, but check dimensions. The Epson ET-2400 is larger than cartridge models.

faq.q: What mistake do home office buyers make?
faq.a: Ignoring running costs. A cheap printer with expensive cartridges costs more over a year.

faq.q: Is the Brother DCP-L2640DW worth it over the Canon TS6520?
faq.a: If you print mainly text and share the machine, yes. For color and a lower price, the Canon wins.

faq.q: How do I set one up?
faq.a: Use the maker's app, such as Canon PRINT or HP Smart, to connect to WiFi and install the driver.

faq.q: How do I stop ink drying out?
faq.a: Print a page regularly. Lasers such as the Brother models avoid the issue because toner does not dry.

faq.q: Can I print from my phone?
faq.a: Yes, wireless models support phone printing. The HL-L2405W lists mobile printing and Alexa compatibility.

finalTake: The Canon PIXMA TS6520 is the best small printer for most home offices because it offers every core function in a compact frame. Pick the Brother DCP-L2640DW for text-heavy work, the Canon TR4720 for paperwork, and the Epson ET-2400 if you print color often.
